expected_effect: Direction: lower public_val_bpb at fixed 1800 s. Predeclared size: steps +3% to +8% over same-host control (about 2130-2240 on trn21, 2140-2245 on trn22) and public_val_bpb lower by 0.001-0.004 (SUCCESS threshold >= 0.001 with steps >= +2%). Quality per step is expected to be unchanged within 0.0005 because logits are rounded from BF16 products accumulated in FP32 and all loss math stays FP32.
hypothesis: Under the pinned control environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS exactly '--optlevel=1', no compiler --auto-cast), the LM-head logits projection [B,T,d] x [d,V] executes with at least one FP32 operand. Because the dense model is only ~55.7M parameters including embeddings (592.9M total minus 537M of ngram-ve tables), the vocab-sized head is a large fraction of dense matmul FLOPs, so an FP32 head is a measurable per-step cost. Executing that single matmul with both operands in BF16 while returning FP32 logits to softcap/CE recovers steps within the fixed 1800 s budget with negligible quality loss, lowering fixed-budget public val_bpb, by the same mechanism that made --bf16-sdpa-input the only KEEP at this commit (2233 vs 2076 steps, 1.002028 vs 1.005967).
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-bf16-lm-head-two-operand-r2 from 9a4caa7b. STEP 0 (static check, recorded in the implementation notes before any edit): locate the final logits projection -- the F.linear / matmul / (tied) wte-weight product mapping the final-normed hidden state [B,T,d] to vocab logits, immediately upstream of the softcap and cross-entropy (region gated by --nki-softcap-ce and --byte-loss-weight). If the head goes through the project's Linear class, read Linear.forward and its weight-cache code and record (a) the dtype of the activation entering the head call, (b) the dtype of the weight tensor actually passed to the matmul (master parameter vs cached copy), (c) whether the cached copy is detached and how gradients reach the FP32 master, (d) whether any torch.autocast context encloses the call, all under default flags (bf16_norm_output False, bf16_sdpa_input False). Quote the line ranges. If both operands are already BF16 or the call is under autocast, stop and return HALT-INERT. STEP 1 (toggle): following the existing --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add module-level USE_BF16_LM_HEAD = True with env override NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_LM_HEAD ('0' disables), argparse pair --bf16-lm-head / --no-bf16-lm-head (dest bf16_lm_head, default None -> constant), and add 'USE_BF16_LM_HEAD' to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES (or the equivalent list that is saved into checkpoints and restored by load_for_eval) so the eval/causality path resolves the same value; default must resolve True so the candidate run uses no flags. STEP 2 (boundary): at the logits projection only, when USE_BF16_LM_HEAD is True, execute: h16 = h.to(torch.bfloat16); w16 = head_weight.to(torch.bfloat16) where head_weight is the FP32 master tensor the current code uses (lm_head.weight or tied wte.weight) -- a differentiable .to() cast, NOT a detached weight-cache copy, so autograd accumulates the FP32 master gradient through the cast; logits = F.linear(h16, w16) (or the equivalent matmul form already used, preserving any transposed-linear layout the code selects, with the transposed mirror also cast via a differentiable .to() if that layout is active); logits = logits.float(). If the existing Linear path already casts the weight to BF16 through a custom autograd function that routes gradients to the master, it is acceptable to reuse that path but the activation cast must be added and the resulting two-operand dtypes must be proven by STEP 4. Leave every downstream operation (softcap, CE, byte-loss weighting, eval BPB accumulation, causality check) untouched so they receive FP32 logits as before. The same forward code serves training and evaluation; no separate eval branch. When USE_BF16_LM_HEAD is False the original call executes unchanged. Do not change tying, create Parameters, or alter initialization, optimizer groups, or grad clipping. STEP 3 (logging): add exactly one field 'bf16_lm_head=<bool>' to the existing precision-options config oneliner. STEP 4 (evidence): add a one-time rank-0 log line at the first head call printing the dtypes of the two matmul operands and of the returned logits (guarded by a module-level flag so it prints once); the smoke log must show bfloat16, bfloat16, float32. STEP 5 (verification for the implementation verifier): (a) diff limited to the toggle/env/CLI resolution, the ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES entry, the head-boundary cast block, the one config-log field, and the one-time dtype log; (b) grep confirms softcap/CE/byte-loss/eval code untouched; (c) with the env override '0' the original path executes; (d) show the checkpoint save/load code path that persists and restores USE_BF16_LM_HEAD for load_for_eval; (e) smoke run resolves bf16_lm_head=True, num_params_M 592.9, ngram_ve and oneliners identical to control, causality_passed True, dtype log as in STEP 4, and meets the smoke gate (>=338 steps, step-rate ratio >=1.01 vs same-host control smoke, public_val_bpb no worse than control smoke +0.003). Record all STEP 0 and STEP 5 artifacts in the experiment directory.
single_causal_change: One numerical-format boundary change confined to train.py: at the LM-head logits projection only, both operands (final-normed hidden activation and the head weight, tied or untied) are temporary BF16 views produced by differentiable .to(torch.bfloat16) casts; the matmul executes in BF16; logits are immediately cast .float() so softcap, cross-entropy, byte-loss weighting, eval BPB accumulation, and the causality check consume FP32 logits byte-for-byte as before. FP32 master parameters, optimizer state, embedding lookup, tying, initialization, all other layers, kernels, schedule, batch, seed, evaluator, launch shape and environment are unchanged; num_params_M must remain 592.9 and the ngram_ve oneliner identical to control. This is a re-proposal of the verifier-PASSED bf16-lm-head concept (never run) that fixes the three implementation-review defects: activation-only cast, absent pre-implementation two-operand dtype/HALT-INERT evidence, and unverified checkpoint/load_for_eval parity. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967). Outcome classes in order: (1) HALT-INERT if the static check finds both head operands already BF16 (or the call under torch.autocast) under default flags; (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control; (4) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if steps > +10% (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22): compare logged validation trajectories at matched step counts before any quality claim; if unavailable, quality attribution is recorded unresolved; SUCCESS only if public_val_bpb < control by >= 0.001 and no matched-step deficit > 0.010 at the control's final step; (5) SUCCESS if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.001; (6) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control; (7) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.
